newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Bank of Cyprus 1995 net profits up 5.4 percent.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Cyprus 1995 net profits up 5.4 percent.

text.p: The Bank of Cyprus, the island's biggest commercial bank, on Friday announced a 5.4 percent increase in its preliminary net profits for 1996, down from a 30 percent jump in 1995.
The bank reported net profits of 24.2 million Cyprus pounds ($47.5 million) in 1996 over 23 million in 1995, when the bank scored a record 30 percent rise over the previous year.

"The year of 1995 was undoubtedly an 'annus mirabilis' for our group and in combination with this year's results the average rate of growth over the past two years was 20 percent, which is considered satisfactory," Solon Triantfyllides, chairman of the Bank of Cyprus Group, told a news conference.

The annual dividend to shareholders remained steady at 18 percent. Preliminary results concerning group operating profit, said Triantafyllides, saw a rise of 8.1 percent to 46.4 million pounds compared to 42.9 million pounds in 1995.

Company figures said the capital base increased 23 percent to 252.6 million pounds last year through the issue of subordinated convertible bonds both in Cyprus and abroad. A rights issue of 25 million pounds is planned in May 1997.
"The increase is considered satisfactory considering the slowdown in economic activity during 1996, particularly the decrease in tourist arrivals," said Triantafyllides.

Last year was generally considered a difficult one because of a slowdown in tourism, the eastern Mediterranean island's main money spinner which provides about 21 percent of GDP. Official figures for tourism are not yet available.
Triantafyllides proposed that the island's central bank, government departments and commercial groups organise roadshows on the benefits of Cyprus as a business centre abroad.
